title: Flat base change preserves Koszul regularity
statement: Let A and S be commutative rings and S a flat A-algebra [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For a finite sequence f:Fin r -> A, if f is Koszul-regular [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], then its image under A -> S is Koszul-regular. The Koszul complex is [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex].

proof.text: In the standard exterior basis, use the contraction formula to express the boundary as a sum over removal of one generator, with coefficient (-1)^(i+2) f_i. Base change the basis and identify it with the exterior basis over S. Applying the ring map to the coefficients identifies the differentials and constructs a complex isomorphism from the tensor product complex to the restriction of the Koszul complex over S.

For each positive degree, the original short complex is exact by Koszul regularity. Tensoring with the flat module S preserves this exactness. Transport exactness through the complex isomorphism, then reflect it along faithful restriction of scalars. The resulting short complex over S is exact, so its homology is zero.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 15.31.5, flat base change; the source argument made explicit in exterior basis coordinates
